title: The Coffee Was There All Along
scene: On a sleepy Sunday morning, you want coffee but find an empty jar. You almost switch to tea, then remember the shopping bag you left by the door.
sceneJa: 日曜の朝。コーヒーを飲もうとしたら容器が空。紅茶に切り替えかけるが、玄関に置いたままの買い物袋を思い出す。小さな発見で、朝の気分が少し上向く。

chunks.ja: 確かに〜だったはずなのに
昨日コーヒーを買ったと
代わりに紅茶をいれるところだった
玄関のそばに置きっぱなしにしていた

chunks.en: the new coffee was still in there,
chunks.ja: 買ったコーヒーはまだその袋に入っていて

chunks.en: I figured I might as well
chunks.ja: せっかくだから〜しておこうと思った

chunks.en: put it in the cupboard now
chunks.ja: 今のうちに戸棚にしまって
また忘れてしまう前に
コーヒーを飲みながら

chunks.en: and feeling oddly proud of myself.
chunks.ja: なぜか少し得意な気分になっていた

questions.question: Which chunking keeps the expression ‘I could've sworn’ together naturally?
options: I could've / sworn I'd / bought coffee / yesterday
I could've sworn / I'd bought coffee yesterday / but the jar was empty
I could've sworn I'd / bought coffee / yesterday but the / jar was empty
questions.explanation: ‘I could've sworn’ is a conversational way to say you were very sure of something, often when the situation seems to contradict your memory. Keep it together.

questions.question: What does ‘I might as well put it in the cupboard now’ mean?
options: I should throw the coffee away immediately.
I have no choice but to buy another bag.
Since the coffee is here, I may as well put it away now.
questions.explanation: ‘Might as well’ suggests doing something because it makes sense in the circumstances, even if it wasn't the original plan.

questions.question: Why does the narrator check the shopping bag?
options: To see whether the coffee they bought is still inside.
To find a receipt to return the coffee.
To check whether the umbrella is broken.
questions.explanation: The narrator remembers buying coffee and checks the bag before giving up and making tea. ‘Just to make sure’ signals a quick confirmation.

speak: Imagine you're getting breakfast ready and can't find something you thought you bought. Round 1: Read ‘I could've sworn / I'd bought coffee yesterday / but the jar was empty’ slowly, pausing at the chunk breaks. Round 2: Stress ‘sworn’ to express surprise, and say ‘It turns out’ with the lighter tone of a discovery. Round 3: Read all six sentences as one small story, shifting from sleepy frustration to amused relief. Speak for 30 seconds: Describe something you thought you'd lost or forgotten. Use ‘I could've sworn ...’, ‘It turns out ...’, and ‘I might as well ...’. Final Read: Read the story again without looking at the Japanese.
review: Revisit Lesson 91: ‘I almost talked myself out of going for a walk’ (散歩をやめかけた) becomes ‘I almost made tea instead’ (代わりに紅茶をいれるところだった)—the same ‘I almost ...’ structure in a new situation. Revisit Lesson 92: ‘Just to make sure’ (念のため) clarified a meeting entrance; here it introduces checking a shopping bag. New chunks: ‘I could've sworn ...’ (確かに〜だったはず), ‘It turns out ...’ (実は〜だと分かった), ‘might as well ...’ (せっかくだから〜しておく).
